body_text:
A *truth assignment* (or valuation) on a set of propositional
variables is a function mapping each variable to one of the
values $\{\text{true}, \text{false}\}$. Any truth assignment
extends uniquely and recursively to all compound formulas
according to the truth tables of their connectives.

A formula is called a *tautology* (or logically valid) if it
evaluates to true under every possible truth assignment; it is
a *contradiction* (or unsatisfiable) if it evaluates to false
under every assignment; and it is *contingent* if it is true
under some assignments and false under others. Tautologies
represent universal logical truths, independent of any factual
state of affairs.
